meta_description: When microseconds and uptime are the product — HPC, low-latency and always-on engineering.

blocks.x: When microseconds and uptime are the product — HPC, low-latency and always-on engineering.

Some systems are the product: matching and pricing engines, grid-adjacent control workloads, real-time bidding, high-throughput risk calculation. We engineer for their physics — latency budgets broken down per hop, kernel-bypass and FPGA accelerators where justified, NUMA-aware placement, and determinism testing under adversarial load. Availability engineering pairs with it: active-active topologies, chaos-verified failover, and capacity headroom policies tied to revenue risk.

HPC workloads (simulation, risk grids, genomic pipelines, CFD) get the same discipline on clusters: scheduler tuning, GPU partitioning, storage tiering for burst patterns, and reproducible environments via containers. Every mission-critical build ships with a load-and-failure evidence pack — the numbers that let the business sign off on what 'always on' actually means.
